item.title: Resynthesising the Traditional: Fragmented Distance (CTM x NOPA Artistic Lab, Armenia)
item.description:
Organisation: CTM Festival with NOPA Festival

Location: Yerevan / Armenia. Preference to artists who reside in or have a diasporic connection to Armenia, Georgia, Iran, Iraq, Syria, the Anatolian region, the Caspian Sea, the Levant, and the Northern Caucasus.

Award: Participants supported with a travel budget of up to EUR 450 each, accommodation and catering for the duration of the lab, a NOPA Festival pass, and a per diem. Visa fees supported when required, and letters of invitation provided. Free to apply.

Duration: Eight-day lab, 1 to 10 October 2026 (arrival 1 October, departure 10 October)

Deadline: Closed 08 Aug 2026

Fragmented Distance is the latest artistic lab from CTM Festival's Resynthesising the Traditional initiative (co-curated by Stas Sharifulla and CTM), taking place 1 to 10 October 2026 in Armenia in collaboration with NOPA, a festival dedicated to sonic arts and experimental music. Resynthesising the Traditional explores how musicians, sound artists, and researchers can critically engage with traditions and heritage, using resynthesis (a computer-music method that analyses sounds to extract their fundamental components) as a guiding metaphor, and resisting conservative views of culture as frozen or untouchable; the lab is an open toolbox helping artists connect to 'the traditional' outside of exoticisation, cultural essentialism, and uneven power dynamics. This edition focuses on diaspora, memory, displacement, transmission, and hybridity, responding to Armenia's shift into a point of arrival for refugees and diasporic communities and to the displacement following the ethnic cleansing of Artsakh / Nagorno-Karabakh. It invites artists whose work resynthesising traditional practices addresses how traditional musical forms are maintained, altered, or recontextualised as they move across geographies and generations, how in-betweenness and non-belonging can be articulated through sound, and how sonic expression can act as rehumanisation. THE LAB (eight days, 10:00-19:00 daily) includes theory and practice workshops, individual closed oral presentations, solo public performances (15-20 minutes), specialist inputs, guided sonic improvisations, field trips, and feedback sessions. Following the lab, participants may propose new solo or collaborative work to the Resynthesising the Traditional team; selected works are shortlisted for commission and presentation at CTM Festival Berlin and/or NOPA Festival Yerevan. CONDITIONS: solo artists/projects only; applicants should have an existing practice tied to (re)connecting with traditional ideas and sounds through a contemporary lens, and clear next steps; working knowledge of English recommended. SELECTION: a pre-selection committee (Varoujan Chetirian, Stas Sharifulla, Taica Replansky) creates a shortlist, from which up to six participants are chosen by lab co-hosts Cinna Peyghamy, Vardan Baghdasaryan, and Varoujan Chetirian. TIMELINE: deadline 8 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST; results by early September 2026; lab 1 to 10 October 2026. Apply with a portfolio (PDF, max 10 pages) and an audio link; questions to team@nopa.art. Free to apply.

item.title: Stichting NORMA: NORMA Fonds Project Grant (round 4, 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Stichting NORMA (collecting society for performing artists)

Location: Netherlands-based arts-sector activity. No city or region restriction stated.

Award: Maximum EUR 10,000 per project. Total project budget may not exceed EUR 150,000 and the applicant organisation's annual budget may not exceed EUR 500,000. At least 25 percent of the project budget must come from audience or box-office revenue. Performer fees must meet the 2026 wage norms of EUR 139 per rehearsal and EUR 340 per performance. No application fee.

Duration: Single project, typically a production or concert series. Final report due within six months of completion.

Deadline: 30 Oct 2026

The NORMA Fonds redistributes copyright remuneration collected by Stichting NORMA into cultural, social and professional projects involving performing artists, and is one of the few Dutch schemes with four intakes a year and a genuinely short cycle. Both arts-sector organisations and individual arts professionals may apply, though the applicant needs a bank account and legal footing and cannot be a BIS-funded institution. The project must centre on performing artists in the copyright sense, meaning people who perform a copyright-protected work: musicians, dancers, actors, voice actors. This fits live experimental music, sound performance and performative media-art work, but not object-based exhibitions or non-performative installation programmes. The maximum grant is EUR 10,000, the total project budget must stay under EUR 150,000, the applicant's annual budget under EUR 500,000, and at least a quarter of the project budget must be earned from audience income, so this is a top-up rather than a primary funding source. Budgets must honour NORMA's 2026 performer wage norms. Applications are submitted online during a one-month window each quarter; the next round runs 1 to 30 October 2026, closing at 23:59. TIMING RULE: decisions arrive no later than eight weeks after the deadline, and the premiere date must fall at least eight weeks after the application deadline. Organisations that already received a NORMA Fonds grant in 2024 or 2025 are excluded, and supporting staff may not exceed 2 FTE.

item.title: University of Amsterdam: PhD, Protest and Political Speech in the Nordics 1930-1970 (Sound of Disagreement)
item.description:
Organisation: University of Amsterdam (UvA), Faculty of Humanities, Department of European Studies

Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands (Kloveniersburgwal 48)

Award: EUR 3,059 to 3,881 gross per month at 38 hours per week, on the Dutch university PhD scale, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and 8.3 percent year-end bonus. No application fee.

Duration: 48 months full-time (16-month initial contract, extended by 32 months after a positive evaluation); preferred start 1 January 2027

Deadline: Closed 20 Aug 2026

Fully funded four-year PhD position within 'The Sound of Disagreement: Embodied Histories of Political Speech 1800-present', an interdisciplinary project on how political groups have argued in public and how disagreement sounds. This sub-project covers Nordic labour movements and the articulation of protest from roughly 1930 to 1970, explicitly working on the sonic practices of political debate and the mediatization of protest, so it suits researchers with a sound studies, media studies or oral history angle as much as historians. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in History, European Studies, Media Studies, Nordic Studies or a related discipline; fluency in Danish, Finnish, Norwegian or Swedish depending on the chosen case study; professional English; archival research skills; and a collaborative disposition. Apply via the AcademicTransfer posting (vacancy number 15290) with a motivation letter, CV and research statement. Deadline 20 August 2026.

item.title: Ernst von Siemens Musikstiftung: Project Funding (October 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Ernst von Siemens Musikstiftung

Location: International, no stated country restriction on the organising institution, though the Foundation is Swiss and German in orientation and administration.

Award: No published minimum or maximum. Primarily covers artistic costs, not overheads. The Foundation explicitly will not fully fund a project, and requires at least one other institution to participate financially at a level similar to the amount requested, functioning as a de facto 1:1 match. No application fee.

Duration: Project-based. The October deadline covers projects beginning the following calendar year.

Deadline: 01 Oct 2026

One of the largest private funders of contemporary and new music in Europe, and it funds the organising side of the field rather than individual artists, which makes it directly usable by festivals. Eligible activity includes festivals, world premieres and revivals, composition commissions, events, academies and workshops, education projects, symposia and musicological publications. Experimental and contemporary sound programming is the core remit; this is not a classical-repertoire fund. There are two annual deadlines: 1 October at 14:00 CEST for projects starting the following year with decisions by year-end, and 1 March for projects starting in July or later with decisions by end of June. Grant sizes are not published, and the Foundation aims funding at artistic rather than overhead costs. Only the organising institution may apply and only legal entities qualify: cultural institutions, orchestra managers, festival organisers and ensembles. Self-applications and applications from individuals are explicitly refused. VOLUME LIMITS are strict and worth planning around: each institution may submit one application per deadline, may be supported for only one project per year, and may be supported for a maximum of three projects across three consecutive years.

item.title: Fundacion Klemm: 29th Premio Klemm a las Artes Visuales 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Fundacion Federico Jorge Klemm

Location: Buenos Aires, Argentina. Open to Argentine nationals and to foreigners with at least two years of legal residence in Argentina.

Award: First acquisition prize ARS 7,000,000 (around USD 4,800), second prize ARS 4,000,000 (around USD 2,750). No entry fee; the foundation pays transport of selected works.

Duration: Single prize with exhibition; submitted work must be dated 2021 or later.

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

The Premio Klemm is one of Argentina's longest-running visual arts prizes, now in its 29th edition, awarded by the Fundacion Federico Jorge Klemm in Buenos Aires. It is notable for a genuinely open definition of medium: the entry categories explicitly include arte digital, robotica, video, videoinstalacion, audio and fotografia alongside painting, drawing and sculpture, so technology-based practice is squarely in scope. Entrants submit one work dated 2021 or later, which must be durable rather than ephemeral. The top prizes are acquisition prizes, so winning work enters the foundation's collection. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: Argentine nationals (native or naturalised) or foreigners holding at least two years of legal residence in Argentina, aged 18 or over. Submissions close 4 September 2026 at 23:59. Prize amounts and the closing date are stated in the bases y condiciones PDF linked from the entry site.

item.title: Klang Copenhagen Avantgarde Music Festival: Open Call 2027, MUSIC/MOVEMENT
item.description:
Organisation: Klang - Copenhagen Avantgarde Music Festival

Location: Dansehallerne, Copenhagen, Denmark. No nationality, age or education restrictions are stated on the call page.

Award: Klang aims to cover production costs and performer fees. Travel and accommodation are discussed case by case rather than guaranteed. No commission fee is offered, since the call seeks finished work rather than new creation. No application fee.

Duration: Performance during Klang Festival 2027, provisional dates 15 to 18 June 2027

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Klang, Copenhagen's avantgarde music festival, is seeking one to three projects at the intersection of experimental music and movement, dance or choreography for its 2027 edition at Dansehallerne. Important constraint: the call is explicitly for ready-to-go projects, not commissions or works in progress, so the work must already be finished and production-ready. Submission is a one-page PDF covering artistic description, budget overview, bios, duration and media links, emailed to opencall@klang.dk with 'Open Call 2027' in the subject line. The submission window runs 1 July to 1 September 2026. The toaspern|moeller duo together with Klang Festival review feasible submissions in September 2026, with notification in October 2026.
